correctness.rationale: For independent bounded mean-one lifetimes Q and lifetime Poisson births rate lambda, total progeny is stochastically dominated by Poisson(lambda B) Galton–Watson; E[N²1_{N>=3}]=O_B(lambda²), so neglecting ≥2 births in E[T], E[S], E[TS] has uniform O_B(lambda²) cost. A single child born at u in ancestor lifetime q, child duration z contributes J(q,z)=∫_0^q(u+z−q)_+du. Exchangeability and J(q,z)+J(z,q)=qz give E J=1/2 and E[(q+z)J]=E Q², so E T=1+lambda/2+O(lambda²), E S=1+lambda+O(lambda²), E TS=E Q²(1+2lambda)+O(lambda²). Thus Cov(T,S)=v+lambda(1/2+2v)+O_B(lambda²). Independent exact rational check for deterministic/two-point Q reproduced derivatives and coefficients.
residual_risks: Small-lambda only and bounded Q; neither arbitrary-rate covariance nor unbounded lifetimes treated.
O_B error is uniform only at fixed common lifetime bound B and sufficiently small lambda.

value.rationale: A natural joint outbreak statistic distinguishes life-duration variance even when the two individual mean observables are insensitive to that distribution. The sharp positive first-order sensitivity 1/2+2v and deterministic equality case provide a concise non-Markovian perturbation law with epidemiological and branching-model motivation.
residual_risks: Only first-order covariance and no complete correlation-function classification are asserted.
